body:
I added a colorscheme picker to my [configuration](https://github.com/pkazmier/nvim/blob/main/lua/plugins/mini/pick.lua) this morning and thought I'd share in case others were interested.  If you preview a colorscheme, it will change your current colorscheme to the one you are previewing. If you cancel the picker, it will revert back to the colorscheme you had before you entered the picker.

https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/assets/747855/a8ae2b11-6998-4034-8fd0-539f8643ecf8

To track state of the original picker, I added the ability to have custom pre- and post-hooks for individual pickers:
```lua
-- Picker pre- and post-hooks ===============================================

-- Keys should be a picker source.name. Value is a callback function that
-- accepts same arguments as User autocommand callback.
local hooks = {
  pre_hooks = {},
  post_hooks = {},
}

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd({ "User" }, {
  pattern = "MiniPickStart",
  group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("minipick-pre-hooks", { clear = true }),
  desc = "Invoke pre_hook for specific picker based on source.name.",
  callback = function(...)
    local opts = MiniPick.get_picker_opts() or {}
    local pre_hook = hooks.pre_hooks[opts.source.name] or function(...) end
    pre_hook(...)
  end,
})

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd({ "User" }, {
  pattern = "MiniPickStop",
  group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("minipick-post-hooks", { clear = true }),
  desc = "Invoke post_hook for specific picker based on source.name.",
  callback = function(...)
    local opts = MiniPick.get_picker_opts() or {}
    local post_hook = hooks.post_hooks[opts.source.name] or function(...) end
    post_hook(...)
  end,
})
```

With that in place, here is the definition of my colorscheme picker:
```lua
-- Colorscheme picker =======================================================

local selected_colorscheme -- Currently selected or original colorscheme

hooks.pre_hooks.Colorschemes = function()
  selected_colorscheme = vim.g.colors_name
end

hooks.post_hooks.Colorschemes = function()
  vim.cmd("colorscheme " .. selected_colorscheme)
end

MiniPick.registry.colorschemes = function()
  local colorschemes = vim.fn.getcompletion("", "color")
  return MiniPick.start({
    source = {
      name = "Colorschemes",
      items = colorschemes,
      choose = function(item)
        selected_colorscheme = item
      end,
      preview = function(buf_id, item)
        vim.cmd("colorscheme " .. item)
        vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf_id, 0, -1, false, { item })
      end,
    },
  })
end
```

reply_data.body:
> I'd also think about applying color scheme not only inside preview, but also after choosing.

It does apply if you choose it.

I don’t explicitly run the colorscheme command in the choose function because it would revert to the original colorscheme that was saved in the pre hook upon exit. The choose function simply sets the name of the selected item and the post hook is where the colorscheme command actually runs. This is how I’m able to revert to the user’s original scheme if they cancel.

reply_data.body:
> The picker for autocommands is even less urgent as I mostly don't see a valid use case for it. What would you expect it to do?

The purpose of the autocommands picker is to provide a way to see which autocommands are currently active and what they are doing. For example, running it would display something like:  

```
CursorMoved          ▏MiniIndentscope             ▏*                         ▏Auto draw indentscope lazily
CursorMoved          ▏MiniCursorword              ▏*                         ▏Auto highlight cursorword
CursorMoved          ▏matchparen                  ▏*                         ▏call s:Highlight_Matching_Pair()
CompleteChanged      ▏IndentBlankline             ▏*                         ▏<lua function>
ColorScheme          ▏MiniStatusline              ▏*                         ▏Ensure colors
...
```

This would help users quickly inspect what autocommands are currently being used, which plugin registered them, and their corresponding actions. It can be useful for debugging and understanding how different plugins interact with events.  

@echasnovski Would this be a valid use case for you?

reply_data.body:
For just examining it can be done with `:au` command (see `:h autocmd-list`). So, something like `:au * <buffer>` will show all autocommands for the current buffer, etc. Yes, it is not as interactive as in picker, but usually gets the job done.

Some of my issues with the dedicated picker for autocommands are:
- There is no suitable "choose" action. The main design of 'mini.pick' is for the picker to be used to *pick* something. The absence of "choose" action somehwat contradicts it.
- I really think that this is a rather niche use case. Not many people want/need to explore currently active autocommands. And for those who do want/need, exploring the `:au` command is even beneficial (at least in long term).

I understand if you think it's unnecessary, but for me, it's more convenient than running `:au`.

comment_data.body:
After several times going back and fourth, I think having relatively concise `colorschemes` picker in 'mini.extra' should be worth it.

@pkazmier, as an original author of this, are you interested in PR? Some notes in advance:
- No need for a general `hooks` approach. A single `MiniPickStop` autocommand with `once = true` that applies `selected_colorscheme` should be enough here (should also take care to not run `:colorscheme` if it not needed, i.e. target color scheme is already applied).
- It would be good to incorporate ['mini.colors' capabilities](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/0429e9ee9d35faef51971abdbb1b26d2540b5a5f/doc/mini-colors.txt#L704) (if it is present) for picker to be able to restore initial state even if there is no `vim.g.colors_name` defined.
- It needs tests for both common and various tricky cases. Like:
    - Navigating up/down with enabled preview should show different previews.
    - Cancelling without choosing should restore original color scheme.
    - Choosing marked should choose first marked item (which is default in 'mini.pick', but should still be tested).
